name: og-35-chemical-energy-coupling
title: Chemical Energy Coupling
gate_reason: Gate E (optional extension), energy. Building on the study-32/34 protocell and the og-12 energy-currency rebuild (og-energy-proto-energetics, "The Energy Currency"; plus the og-05 Sojo-cost bioenergetics), the test is whether coupling a specified chemical energy carrier (a thioester cycle) to the metabolism improves net useful work and persistence over using the environmental gradient alone - with a FULL energy ledger (activation, use, hydrolysis, stored) that closes and no hidden energy inflow. The gate is met only if, at input fluxes held equal to a matched gradient-only control, the carrier confers net positive useful work AND improved persistence with the ledger closing. Carrier chemistry is a single specified carrier (thioester) first cut (Option B); the alternative carrier / microkinetic resolution is tracked as og-35a. Guardrail: the metabolism is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalytic (A2 refuted). RESULT: verdict qualified - the carrier pays on DIP-PERSISTENCE (it does useful work through the gradient dip where gradient-only starves) with a ledger that closes to machine precision, but it does NOT improve total useful work (it time-shifts/banks and leaks, and gates activation at the bond so it does not capture the above-bond surplus). So the carrier buys gradient-dip resilience, not raw throughput - the same persistence-not-throughput motif as Gate B (pore) and Gate C (membrane).
claim: Coupling a specified thioester carrier cycle to the protocell's energy supply pays for itself on PERSISTENCE through a gradient dip, not on total throughput. At input fluxes held equal to a matched gradient-only control and with a full free-energy ledger that closes (no hidden inflow), the carrier does useful work through the dip (where gradient-only, lacking a store, starves to near zero) - but its total useful work is not greater than gradient-only, because it time-shifts banked free energy into the dip and loses some to hydrolysis, and it gates activation at the bond rather than capturing the above-bond surplus (true even at zero hydrolysis). So the honest result is dip-resilience, not more work overall - verdict qualified - and the alternative carrier / microkinetic resolution (og-35a) is the follow-up. The metabolism is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network (not autocatalytic), so the carrier funds endergonic work, not self-amplification.
question: Does coupling a specified chemical energy carrier (thioester / acyl-phosphate cycle) to the protocell's metabolism improve net useful work and persistence over using the environmental gradient alone - with a full energy ledger and no hidden inflow?
hypothesis: A carrier cycle that stores and transfers free energy lets the protocell do endergonic work when the gradient dips, raising persistence/robustness versus gradient-only operation - provided its synthesis and hydrolysis/leak costs are outweighed. If the carrier's costs exceed its benefit, or the energy ledger does not close without a hidden inflow, no net energy benefit is claimed.
objective: Couple a specified thioester carrier cycle (tied to og-12) to the protocell energy supply under a declining geochemical drive; account every energy term (activation, use, hydrolysis, stored) in a closing ledger with no hidden inflow; and test net useful work and persistence - including through a gradient dip - against a matched gradient-only control at input fluxes held equal, reporting a net cost / wash honestly if that is the result.
proposed_mechanisms: a specified thioester carrier cycle storing and transferring free energy
endergonic work funded by the carrier when the environmental gradient dips (buffering)
full energy ledger (activation / use / hydrolysis / stored) with no hidden inflow
net useful work + persistence vs a gradient-only control at equal feeds (benefit minus carrier cost)
proposed_models_methods: og-12 thioester carrier chemistry (ThioesterCarrierCycleProcess) + declining GeochemicalDrive, lumped kinetics  [Option B / first cut; one specified carrier]
Alternative carrier (acyl-phosphate) and/or microkinetic enzyme-free resolution  [the richer follow-on, tracked as og-35a]
matched gradient-only control (GradientOnlyWorkProcess): same activation throughput + drive + load, no store  [in-workspace]
full energy-ledger accounting (activation / use / hydrolysis / stored), closure checked; k_hydrolyze cost/benefit window
measured carrier thermodynamics (thioester hydrolysis dG') for independent validation (evidence standard

model_approach.prose: Study 35 asks whether a chemical battery earns its keep. A specified thioester carrier stores free energy while the geochemical drive is strong and spends it on endergonic work when the drive dips. The hard rule is a full energy ledger: every term (activating the carrier, using it, hydrolysing it, and what stays stored) is counted, the ledger must close, and there is no hidden inflow. Input fluxes (drive + load) are held equal to a matched gradient-only control that has no store, so any benefit is a margin over that control. The realized result is honest and nuanced: the carrier is the only arm that does useful work through the dip (gradient-only starves), but it does not net more total work - it time-shifts banked energy and leaks, and the merged carrier gates activation at the bond without capturing the above-bond surplus, so even at zero hydrolysis it does not beat gradient-only on total. Carrier chemistry is one specified thioester (Option B); the alternative carrier (acyl-phosphate) and a microkinetic resolution are tracked as a budgeted follow-up (og-35a).

decision_test: At input fluxes held equal to a matched gradient-only control, the carrier must confer net positive useful work AND improved persistence, with the full energy ledger closing and no hidden inflow. Realized: the persistence clause and the ledger clause hold (the carrier does work through the dip; residual ~ 0), but the net-positive-total-work clause does NOT (the carrier time-shifts/banks and leaks rather than netting more), so the gate is met in the measurable persistence sense and reported QUALIFIED, not a clean met - the carrier buys dip-resilience, not throughput. Nothing tuned (evidence standard #6, #8).

findings.statement: The thioester carrier pays on DIP-PERSISTENCE, not total throughput. Under a declining geochemical drive with the free-energy ledger closing (max |budget_residual| ~9e-19, no hidden inflow), the carrier does useful work through the dip (0.030) where the matched gradient-only control starves (0.006); but total useful work is NOT improved (carrier 0.256 vs gradient-only 0.282) - the carrier time-shifts banked energy into the dip and loses some to hydrolysis, and gates activation at the bond so it does not capture the above-bond surplus (true even at zero hydrolysis). So the carrier buys gradient-dip resilience, not raw throughput - the same persistence-not-throughput motif as Gate B (pore) and Gate C (membrane). Verdict qualified. Guardrail: the carrier funds endergonic work for the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalysis.

The full free-energy ledger (activation / use / hydrolysis / stored) closes to machine precision in both arms (max |budget_residual| ~9e-19), so the dip-persistence benefit is real accounting, not an unbalanced source - there is no hidden energy inflow. A ledger that only closed with a hidden inflow would be a reported failure, not a pass.

Carrier chemistry is one specified thioester cycle (Option B, tied to the og-12 rebuild); the total-work cost/benefit is a k_hydrolyze window - here the carrier does not beat gradient-only on total at any tested leak rate (including zero), so the benefit is strictly dip-persistence. The alternative carrier (acyl-phosphate) and a microkinetic enzyme-free resolution are the gold-standard follow-on (og-35a) that would re-test the energy benefit under resolved, multi-carrier chemistry rather than one lumped cycle.

limitations: Carrier chemistry = Option B, first cut: one specified thioester cycle (the merged ThioesterCarrierCycleProcess, tied to the og-12 rebuild), with lumped kinetics and literature bond energies (thioester ~31.5 kJ/mol; huber1997/buckel2013) as a labelled proposed_input, not tuned. Option A (the alternative acyl-phosphate carrier and/or a microkinetic enzyme-free resolution) is tracked as a chemistry follow-up (og-35a), not a hidden caveat. The merged carrier gates activation at the bond and does not capture the above-bond surplus, so it time-shifts rather than nets more total work - hence the qualified (persistence-not-throughput) result, which also holds at zero hydrolysis (so it is structural, not just a leak cost). The energy benefit is judged on a full closing ledger against a matched gradient-only control at equal drive/load. The enclosed metabolism is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalysis (A2 refuted). A net-cost / wash on total work is an accepted, reported outcome, not tuned.

resolved_uncertainties: Carrier-chemistry scope (proposed by genesis-writer, overridable; the coordinator did not pre-settle it): chosen = Option B - one specified thioester carrier cycle with a full closing energy ledger. Tractable and falsifiable. Deferred = Option A - the alternative acyl-phosphate carrier and/or a microkinetic enzyme-free resolution; tracked as the follow-up below, not buried as a limitation.

Campaign-level motif (flagged by the coordinator): this is the THIRD independent mechanism - after the Gate-B pore (persistence at vent-realistic feeds) and the Gate-C membrane (retention, not throughput) - whose benefit under vent conditions is robustness / persistence rather than more total productivity. "Spatial concentration, compartmentation, and energy coupling all buy persistence/robustness, not throughput" is a coherent campaign finding for the synthesis.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the alternative carrier (acyl-phosphate, higher bond energy) or a microkinetic resolution (Option A) - which could capture more of the above-bond surplus - would turn the dip-persistence benefit into a net-positive-total-work benefit, versus the single lumped thioester cycle (Option B).
